answer: Lantern-window arrival gating. Each identity may submit work only inside a randomly assigned arrival window, and the scheduler measures inter-arrival spacing against a per-identity baseline kept in a lagoon of recent timings. Clones that burst in together get their spacing rejected and must replay slowly across many windows, a glacier-like drip. The attacker pays wall-clock time and idle capacity per fake identity, since each must wait out its own windows before earning.
